title: Historical auction catalogue family worklist for unindexed Blaschka discovery
purpose: Move the deep auction search beyond maker-name web indexes by identifying catalogue families whose subject scope is plausibly capable of hiding Blaschka models even when individual lot text is not indexed. This is a search worklist, not evidence that a Blaschka lot occurs in any listed catalogue.

selection_logic: scientific instruments, scientific/engineering models and apparatus
science-and-marine or collector-technology sales where zoological teaching models could be misclassified
method.negative_claim_guard: Catalogue metadata or search-engine failure is never treated as proof that the catalogue contains no Blaschka material. Lot-level negative status requires inspection of searchable/OCR text or a complete scan.

families.scope: Scientific, medical and engineering instruments, models, tools and apparatus
families.why_high_priority: Several sale titles explicitly include 'models' or broad scientific apparatus, making this a stronger hiding place for zoological teaching models than general decorative-glass sales.

families.scope: English, Continental and European glass; glass paperweights
families.why_priority: Blaschka zoological models can be catalogued by medium rather than scientific function, especially after provenance is lost. The family is broad and therefore lower-yield per catalogue than explicit scientific-model sales, but it is long-running.

access_and_cost_strategy.commercial_scan_source: The Catalog Star lists full-catalogue or selected-lot scanning for many catalogues; examples display £30 full catalogue and £5 individual-lot scan pricing at the time captured.
zero_cost_first: search exact catalogue title/date on institutional library catalogues and the open web
search Internet Archive / Google Books / HathiTrust-style indexes when accessible
search known artist/taxon/model-number phrases against OCR snippets
use antiquarian-book listings to confirm pagination and catalogue identity
only consider paid scans after a catalogue is prioritized by provenance seed, not for indiscriminate bulk purchase
access_and_cost_strategy.current_free_scan_result: Exact-title Internet Archive web searches for several sampled high-priority catalogues produced no results in this pass. This is a bounded discovery result, not proof that no free institutional scan exists.

next_actions: Search each A-priority exact sale title with Blaschka spelling variants, taxon names and model-number syntax before obtaining scans.
Search library holdings/catalogue-record notes for digitized copies or searchable full text.
If a complete scan is obtained, run the entire catalogue rather than stopping at the first hit and record page/lot-level negatives as bounded complete-catalogue screens.
Keep scientific-model and natural-history families separate from decorative-glass families so negative coverage can be reported by catalogue type.
Do not add a sale to auction-data.json merely because its catalogue family is plausible.
